questions.title: Rescue Division By Zero
questions.description:
Read two integers a and b, then print a/b. If b is 0, print `Error: Division by zero` instead.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer a. Line 2: integer b.

Output Format:
Either the integer quotient or `Error: Division by zero`.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a, b <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
a = gets.to_i
b = gets.to_i
begin
  puts a / b
rescue ZeroDivisionError
  puts "Error: Division by zero"
end

questions.title: Ensure Cleanup Message
questions.description:
Read an integer n. If n is negative, raise `Negative input`. In all cases, the `ensure` clause must print `Finalized` after the main logic.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.

Output Format:
Either `Processed: N` then `Finalized`, or `Error: Negative input` then `Finalized`.

Constraints:
-1000 <= n <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
begin
  raise "Negative input" if n < 0
  puts "Processed: #{n}"
rescue => e
  puts "Error: #{e.message}"
ensure
  puts "Finalized"
end

questions.title: Else Clause Demo
questions.description:
Read a line of input and try to parse it as an integer with `Integer(input)`. If parsing succeeds (no exception), the `else` clause prints `No error`. If parsing fails, print `Not a number`.

Input Format:
Line 1: a token (integer or non-numeric string).

Output Format:
`Parsed: N` followed by `No error` on success; otherwise `Not a number`.

Constraints:
Token length 1..20.
questions.sourcecode:
input = gets.chomp
begin
  n = Integer(input)
  puts "Parsed: #{n}"
rescue ArgumentError
  puts "Not a number"
else
  puts "No error"
end

questions.title: Raise On Invalid Age
questions.description:
Read an integer age. If age is negative or greater than 150, raise a RuntimeError with message `Invalid age`. Otherwise print `Age: N`.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer age.

Output Format:
Either `Age: N` or `Invalid age`.

Constraints:
-1000 <= age <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
age = gets.to_i
begin
  raise "Invalid age" if age < 0 || age > 150
  puts "Age: #{age}"
rescue => e
  puts e.message
end

questions.title: Custom Exception Class
questions.description:
Define a custom exception `InvalidCodeError` (subclass of `StandardError`). Validate that an input code has length between 4 and 12 inclusive. Print `Valid` if so, otherwise the raised error message.

Input Format:
Line 1: a code string.

Output Format:
`Valid` or one of `Code too short` / `Code too long`.

Constraints:
Code length 1..30.
questions.sourcecode:
class InvalidCodeError < StandardError; end

def validate(code)
  raise InvalidCodeError, "Code too short" if code.length < 4
  raise InvalidCodeError, "Code too long" if code.length > 12
  "Valid"
end

code = gets.chomp
begin
  puts validate(code)
rescue InvalidCodeError => e
  puts e.message
end

questions.title: Retry On Failed Read
questions.description:
Read an integer n. Simulate a flaky first attempt: the first time the begin block runs it raises an error, on the second attempt it succeeds. Use `retry` to make a second attempt.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.

Output Format:
`Got N after 2 tries`.

Constraints:
-1000 <= n <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
attempts = 0
n = gets.to_i
begin
  attempts += 1
  raise "simulate failure" if attempts < 2
  puts "Got #{n} after #{attempts} tries"
rescue
  retry if attempts < 3
  puts "Failed"
end

questions.title: ATM Withdrawal Rescue
questions.description:
An ATM dispenses cash only if the amount does not exceed the balance. Define a custom `InsufficientFundsError` and rescue it.

Input Format:
Line 1: float balance. Line 2: float amount.

Output Format:
Either the new balance (2 decimals) or `Insufficient funds`.

Constraints:
0.0 <= balance, amount <= 100000.0.
questions.sourcecode:
class InsufficientFundsError < StandardError; end

balance = gets.to_f
amount = gets.to_f
begin
  raise InsufficientFundsError if amount > balance
  balance -= amount
  puts "%.2f" % balance
rescue InsufficientFundsError
  puts "Insufficient funds"
end

questions.title: Config Parse Ensure Finish
questions.description:
A configuration line is comma-separated. Split it, and ensure the loader prints `Config load finished` regardless of outcome. Reject configs with fewer than 2 fields.

Input Format:
Line 1: comma-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Either the joined tokens (with ` | `) followed by `Config load finished`, or `Parse error: Missing values` followed by `Config load finished`.

Constraints:
Line length 1..200.
questions.sampleoutput1:
a | b | c
Config load finished
questions.sampleoutput2:
Parse error: Missing values
Config load finished
questions.output2:
one | two | three | four
Config load finished
questions.output3:
Parse error: Missing values
Config load finished
questions.sourcecode:
raw = gets.chomp
begin
  parts = raw.split(",")
  raise "Missing values" if parts.size < 2
  puts parts.map(&:strip).join(" | ")
rescue => e
  puts "Parse error: #{e.message}"
ensure
  puts "Config load finished"
end

questions.title: Number Parser With Else
questions.description:
Given a line of whitespace-separated tokens, count how many parse as integers and how many fail. Use a `begin/rescue/else` block per token.

Input Format:
Line 1: space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Line 1: `Valid: V`. Line 2: `Invalid: I`.

Constraints:
1 <= token count <= 100.
questions.sourcecode:
tokens = gets.split
valid = 0
invalid = 0
tokens.each do |t|
  begin
    n = Integer(t)
  rescue ArgumentError
    invalid += 1
  else
    valid += 1
  end
end
puts "Valid: #{valid}"
puts "Invalid: #{invalid}"

questions.title: Profit Share Division Rescue
questions.description:
Partners in a startup share a quarterly profit equally. If the partner count is zero, print `No partners to share with`.

Input Format:
Line 1: float profit. Line 2: integer partners.

Output Format:
Either `Each gets X.XX` or `No partners to share with`.

Constraints:
0.0 <= profit <= 1000000.0; 0 <= partners <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
profit = gets.to_f
partners = gets.to_i
begin
  raise ZeroDivisionError if partners.zero?
  share = profit / partners
  puts "Each gets %.2f" % share
rescue ZeroDivisionError
  puts "No partners to share with"
end

questions.title: Inventory Validation Raise
questions.description:
A warehouse log records items as `name qty`. Validate each entry: qty must be 0..1000. Use custom exception classes; rescue and aggregate the valid/invalid lists.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: `name qty` separated by space.

Output Format:
Line 1: comma-separated `name:qty` of valid items. Line 2: comma-separated error messages for invalid items.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; -1000 <= qty <= 10000; name length 1..20.
questions.sourcecode:
class InvalidQuantityError < StandardError; end
class InvalidNameError < StandardError; end

n = gets.to_i
valid = []
invalid = []
n.times do
  line = gets.chomp
  parts = line.split
  name = parts[0]
  qty = parts[1].to_i
  begin
    raise InvalidNameError, "Bad name: #{name}" if name.nil? || name.empty?
    raise InvalidQuantityError, "Bad qty: #{qty}" if qty < 0 || qty > 1000
    valid << "#{name}:#{qty}"
  rescue InvalidNameError, InvalidQuantityError => e
    invalid << e.message
  end
end
puts valid.join(", ")
puts invalid.join(", ")

questions.title: Connection Retry With Limit
questions.description:
A flaky network call must succeed on a target attempt number. Retry the begin block until the target is reached or the max attempts (3) is exhausted.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer target (the attempt number on which the call succeeds).

Output Format:
Either `Connected on attempt K` or `Failed after 3 attempts`.

Constraints:
1 <= target <= 10.
questions.sourcecode:
max_attempts = 3
attempts = 0
target = gets.to_i
begin
  attempts += 1
  raise "Connection failed" unless attempts >= target
  puts "Connected on attempt #{attempts}"
rescue => e
  if attempts < max_attempts
    retry
  else
    puts "Failed after #{attempts} attempts"
  end
end

questions.title: Parse Integers With Custom Exception
questions.description:
Parse a list of tokens as integers. For each non-integer token, raise a custom `ParseError` carrying the bad token, then rescue it and skip.

Input Format:
Line 1: space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Line 1: `Sum: S`. Line 2: `Parsed: P` (count of successfully parsed integers).

Constraints:
1 <= token count <= 100; token length 1..20.
questions.sampleoutput1:
Skipped: abc
Skipped: xyz
Sum: 35
Parsed: 3
questions.output1:
Skipped: a
Skipped: b
Skipped: c
Sum: 0
Parsed: 0
questions.output3:
Skipped: hello
Skipped: world
Sum: 6
Parsed: 3
questions.sourcecode:
class ParseError < StandardError
  attr_reader :token
  def initialize(token)
    @token = token
    super("Cannot parse: #{token}")
  end
end

def parse_token(t)
  Integer(t)
rescue ArgumentError
  raise ParseError, t
end

tokens = gets.split
total = 0
parsed = 0
tokens.each do |t|
  begin
    n = parse_token(t)
    total += n
    parsed += 1
  rescue ParseError => e
    puts "Skipped: #{e.token}"
  end
end
puts "Sum: #{total}"
puts "Parsed: #{parsed}"

questions.title: Bank Account Ensure Logging
questions.description:
A bank splits (balance + bonus) equally among partners. If partners is 0, rescue the ZeroDivisionError. The `ensure` clause always prints `Transaction closed`.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer balance. Line 2: integer partners. Line 3: integer bonus.

Output Format:
Line 1: `Each gets X` (integer share) or `No partners to share with`. Line 2: `Transaction closed`.

Constraints:
0 <= balance, bonus, partners <= 100000.
questions.sampleoutput2:
No partners to share with
Transaction closed
questions.output2:
No partners to share with
Transaction closed
questions.sourcecode:
balance = gets.to_i
partners = gets.to_i
bonus = gets.to_i
begin
  share = (balance + bonus) / partners
  puts "Each gets #{share}"
rescue ZeroDivisionError
  puts "No partners to share with"

  puts "Transaction closed"

questions.title: Re-raise After Logging
questions.description:
An inner `compute(a, b)` method divides a by b. On ZeroDivisionError it logs the error class and re-raises. The outer caller catches the re-raised exception.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer a. Line 2: integer b.

Output Format:
Either `Computed: Q` (the quotient), or two lines: `Logging: ZeroDivisionError` then `Caught at top level`.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a, b <= 1000.
questions.sampleoutput2:
Logging: ZeroDivisionError
Caught at top level
questions.output2:
Logging: ZeroDivisionError
Caught at top level
questions.sourcecode:
def compute(a, b)
  result = a / b
  puts "Computed: #{result}"
rescue ZeroDivisionError => e
  puts "Logging: #{e.class}"
  raise
end

a = gets.to_i
b = gets.to_i
begin
  compute(a, b)
rescue ZeroDivisionError
  puts "Caught at top level"
end

questions.title: Custom Exception Hierarchy
questions.description:
Define a hierarchy of custom exceptions: `AppError` (base), `NetworkError`, `AuthError`. The `perform(action)` method raises the appropriate one. Rescue each separately and print a tailored message.

Input Format:
Line 1: action (`network`, `auth`, or `other`).

Output Format:
`Network issue: ...` / `Auth issue: ...` / `App issue: ...`.

Constraints:
Action is one of {network, auth, other}.
questions.inputconstrains: Action is one of {network, auth, other}
questions.sourcecode:
class AppError < StandardError; end
class NetworkError < AppError; end
class AuthError < AppError; end

def perform(action)
  case action
  when "network" then raise NetworkError, "Network unreachable"
  when "auth" then raise AuthError, "Bad credentials"
  else raise AppError, "Unknown error"
  end
end

action = gets.chomp
begin
  perform(action)
  puts "Action succeeded"
rescue NetworkError => e
  puts "Network issue: #{e.message}"
rescue AuthError => e
  puts "Auth issue: #{e.message}"
rescue AppError => e
  puts "App issue: #{e.message}"
end

questions.title: Retry With Exponential Backoff
questions.description:
A retry loop attempts to connect. The call succeeds once `attempts >= target`. On each failure the total backoff grows by `2**(attempt-1)`. Stop retrying after `max_attempts` tries.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer max_attempts (1..5). Line 2: integer target (1..10).

Output Format:
Either `Connected after K attempt(s), total backoff B` or `Gave up after K attempt(s), total backoff B`.

Constraints:
1 <= max_attempts <= 5; 1 <= target <= 10.
questions.output1: Gave up after 2 attempt(s), total backoff 1
questions.sourcecode:
max_attempts = gets.to_i
target = gets.to_i
attempts = 0
backoff = 0
begin
  attempts += 1
  raise "Not yet" unless attempts >= target
  puts "Connected after #{attempts} attempt(s), total backoff #{backoff}"
rescue => e
  if attempts < max_attempts
    backoff += 2 ** (attempts - 1)
    retry
  else
    puts "Gave up after #{attempts} attempt(s), total backoff #{backoff}"
  end
end

questions.title: Multi-Step Pipeline With Exception Aggregation
questions.description:
A pipeline applies three steps to each input integer: double it (raise if input negative), add one (raise if doubled result exceeds 1000), then stringify (raise if value is 0). Aggregate successes and failures across all inputs.

Input Format:
Line 1: space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: semicolon-separated `Result: X` strings of successful runs. Line 2: semicolon-separated failure messages.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; -1000 <= v <= 10000.
questions.sampleoutput2:
Result: 11
Step double failed on -1: negative; Step add_one failed on 2002: overflow
questions.sourcecode:
class StepError < StandardError
  attr_reader :step, :input
  def initialize(step, input, msg)
    @step = step
    @input = input
    super("Step #{step} failed on #{input}: #{msg}")
  end
end

def step_double(x)
  raise StepError.new("double", x, "negative") if x < 0
  x * 2
end

def step_add_one(x)
  raise StepError.new("add_one", x, "overflow") if x > 1000
  x + 1
end

def step_to_s(x)
  raise StepError.new("to_s", x, "zero") if x == 0
  "Result: #{x}"
end

nums = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
results = []
errors = []
nums.each do |x|
  begin
    r = step_double(x)
    r = step_add_one(r)
    r = step_to_s(r)
    results << r
  rescue StepError => e
    errors << e.message
  end
end
puts results.join("; ")
puts errors.join("; ")

questions.title: Transaction Rollback With Ensure
questions.description:
A ledger transaction debits then credits the balance. If debit exceeds balance, raise `Overdraft` and restore the original balance via the rescue clause. The `ensure` clause always prints the final balance.

Input Format:
Line 1: float balance. Line 2: float debit. Line 3: float credit.

Output Format:
Either `New balance: X.XX` followed by `Final balance: X.XX`, or `Rolled back: Overdraft` followed by `Final balance: X.XX`.

Constraints:
0.0 <= balance <= 100000.0; 0.0 <= debit, credit <= 100000.0.
questions.sourcecode:
balance = gets.to_f
debit = gets.to_f
credit = gets.to_f
original_balance = balance
begin
  raise "Overdraft" if debit > balance
  balance -= debit
  balance += credit
  puts "New balance: #{"%.2f" % balance}"
rescue => e
  balance = original_balance
  puts "Rolled back: #{e.message}"
ensure
  puts "Final balance: #{"%.2f" % balance}"
end

questions.title: Chained Custom Exceptions With Cause
questions.description:
A two-stage validation parses raw CSV input via `load_data` (raises `DataLoadError`) and `validate` (raises `ValidationError`). Rescue each separately and print a tailored message.

Input Format:
Line 1: comma-separated tokens (single token if no comma).

Output Format:
`Valid: T1, T2, ...` or `Load failed: ...` or `Validation failed: ...`.

Constraints:
Line length 1..200.
questions.sampleoutput2: Validation failed: Need at least 2 items
questions.sourcecode:
class DataLoadError < StandardError; end
class ValidationError < StandardError; end

def load_data(raw)
  raise DataLoadError, "Empty input" if raw.strip.empty?
  raw.split(",").map(&:strip)
end

def validate(items)
  raise ValidationError, "Need at least 2 items" if items.size < 2
  raise ValidationError, "Item too long" if items.any? { |i| i.length > 10 }
  items
end

raw = gets.chomp
begin
  items = load_data(raw)
  validated = validate(items)
  puts "Valid: #{validated.join(", ")}"
rescue DataLoadError => e
  puts "Load failed: #{e.message}"
rescue ValidationError => e
  puts "Validation failed: #{e.message}"
end
